summary: Ikuro Hattori works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Holding a Ph.D. from Pune University, he has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2003, 2026) and served as a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2026).

Ildikó Puskás (1942–2009) specialized in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied under János Harmatta from circa 1963 to 1968 and held a post at Eötvös Loránd University from circa 1968 to 2008.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a religious studies scholar who studied under René Gothóni. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki in 1984 and as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

Ilya Gershevitch (1914–2001) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied under Antonino Pagliaro, Walter Bruno Henning, and Harold Walter Bailey, later teaching at Cambridge (1948–1965) and Columbia University (1960–1961).

Immanuel Bekker (1785–1871) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1803–1807), taught Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1810 to 1871.
Imran Philip works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies under Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (both attested 2026).

Imre Bangha (born 1967) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University (PhD 1998), holding posts at Visva-Bharati, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Oxford as Associate Professor of Hindi.

Imre Galambos (born 1967) works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. A UC Berkeley PhD (circa 2002), he held posts at the British Library, Cambridge (2012–2023), Hamburg (circa 2023), and Zhejiang University (circa 2023).

Imre Hamar (born 1967) studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under advisor Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006 and has served as a visiting professor at Otani University.

Imtiyaz Yusuf works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from Temple University (1984–1990) and served as a professor at the International Islamic University Malaysia in 2019.

In-gun Kang is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, the Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, and Heythrop College under Michael Barnes (attested 2012).

Indira Viswanathan Peterson (born 1950) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard (circa 1971–1976). She held posts at Columbia University and Mount Holyoke College (circa 1989–2019).

Ines Konczak-Nagel is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at Berlin State Museums, Ryukoku University (2012), the Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Leipzig University (attested 2026).
Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University in 2005 and pursued PhD candidacy at the University of Bristol (attested 2012).

Ingo Strauch specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2000, he taught at Berlin (attested 2008) and became a professor at the University of Lausanne in 2012.
Inyoung Chung is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Mihălcescu (1874–1948) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Bucharest, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. 1901–1904), later becoming a Privatdozent at Bucharest in 1904.

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Mircea Eliade and held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1976–1986) and the University of Chicago Divinity School (1986–1991).
Iona Macgregor works in Indology and linguistics. She studied and held a post as a project staff member (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Ippei Okamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at Toyo University (attested 2014) and served as a visiting researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
